diagnosis: The route verifies that key_id belongs to service_account_id sa_id, but never checks whether sa_id belongs to current_user.organization_id. Any authenticated user can revoke service account API keys belonging to other organizations, causing service outages for backend integrations.
exploit_request:
DELETE /api/v1/service-accounts/sa_prod_billing_daemon/api-keys/sak_99210 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <attacker_token>
corrected_code:
@router.delete("/api/v1/service-accounts/{sa_id}/api-keys/{key_id}")
async def revoke_service_account_key(
    sa_id: str,
    key_id: str,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    stmt = (
        select(ServiceAccountKey)
        .join(ServiceAccount)
        .where(
            ServiceAccountKey.id == key_id,
            ServiceAccountKey.service_account_id == sa_id,
            ServiceAccount.organization_id == current_user.organization_id
        )
    )
    res = await db.execute(stmt)
    key = res.scalar_one_or_none()
    if not key:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Service account key not found or unauthorized")
    key.is_revoked = True
    await db.commit()
    return {"status": "revoked", "key_id": key_id}
